items.description: Analyze repository structure, tooling capabilities, and agent architecture
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/repo_analysis.md documenting: (a) all modules and their purposes (.archivara/concept_evolve.py, .archivara/semantic_scholar.py, .opencode/ wrappers), (b) available tool commands (concept_evolve: evolve/probe/reframe/walk; semantic_scholar: search/citations/references/recommend/graph/bibtex), (c) agent permission matrix from .archivara/opencode.json (orchestrator/researcher/writer/reviewer/concept_worker roles), (d) planned output directory structure under results/ and figures/. File must be at least 200 lines and include a dependency diagram of which rubric items feed into which.

items.description: Conduct exhaustive literature search on univalent Bloch constant via web search and Semantic Scholar
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute at least 12 distinct searches using Semantic Scholar (search command) and web search for: (1) 'univalent Bloch constant', (2) 'schlicht Bloch constant lower bound', (3) 'Skinner univalent Bloch 2009', (4) 'Carroll Ortega-Cerda univalent Bloch-Landau harmonic symmetry', (5) 'Beller Hummel univalent Bloch 1985', (6) 'Goodman Bloch-Landau schlicht domains 1945', (7) 'Yanagihara locally univalent Bloch constant', (8) 'Bonk Chen Gauthier Xiong Bloch constant improvement', (9) 'Polya Chebotarev problem minimal capacity continuum', (10) 'conformal welding extremal domains', (11) 'Rettinger computability Bloch Landau constant', (12) 'Beardon Minda Schwarz-Pick Bloch'. Collect at least 20 distinct relevant papers. Record in results/phase1/literature_search_log.json with query, source, and key findings per entry.

items.description: Create and maintain sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: File sources.bib exists at repo root with valid BibTeX entries for at least 20 relevant papers including all of: Skinner2009, Yanagihara1995, BhowmikSen2023a, BhowmikSen2023b, BellerHummel1985, CarrollOrtegaCerda2009, Goodman1945, ChenShiba2004, Bonk1990, ChenGauthier1996, Xiong1998, AhlforsGrunsky1937, Ahlfors1938, Rademacher1943, Minda1982a, Minda1982b, Robinson1935, Rettinger2008, Rettinger2012, OrtegaCerdaPridhnani2008. Each entry must have author, title, journal/venue, year, and DOI or URL where available. Entries must be syntactically valid BibTeX.

items.description: Deep-dive: Skinner's 2009 method (current best lower bound B_u > 0.5708858)
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/skinner_method_analysis.md containing: (a) precise statement of Skinner's theorem with all hypotheses, (b) reconstruction of the proof strategy: subordination argument, the auxiliary function B(r) bounding |f(z)| from below for |z|=r, the implicit improvement function C(r) >= B(r), and extraction of the numerical constant, (c) identification of the exact inequalities where tightness is lost (Koebe distortion, growth theorem, area theorem applications), (d) comparison with Beller-Hummel 1985 approach (coefficient-based vs. subordination-based), (e) at least 5 specific mathematical bottlenecks that if resolved would yield a tighter bound, ranked by estimated impact. Must cite [Skin2009] and [BellerHummel1985] from sources.bib. At least 300 lines.

items.description: Deep-dive: Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2009 upper bound B_u <= 0.6564 via harmonic symmetry and conformal welding
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/upper_bound_analysis.md covering: (a) Goodman's 1945 original domain construction for upper bounds on the schlicht Bloch constant, (b) Carroll-Ortega-Cerda's 2009 construction: the slit-disk domain with harmonic symmetry in each slit arc w.r.t. the origin, (c) the role of Fedorov's solution to the Polya-Chebotarev problem for 4 symmetrically placed points, (d) the conformal welding technique used to prove existence, (e) the precise numerical value 0.6564 and how it is computed, (f) gap analysis: the interval (0.5708858, 0.6564) has width ~0.0855, identifying which end is likely closer to truth, (g) strategies for tightening the upper bound by optimizing slit configurations. Must reference at least 5 papers from sources.bib. At least 250 lines.

items.description: Use literature-graph-miner subagent to mine citation graphs of key papers for cross-domain transferable techniques
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to literature-graph-miner subagent with seed papers: Skinner2009, CarrollOrtegaCerda2009, BellerHummel1985, Ahlfors1938, ChenGauthier1996. Use Semantic Scholar graph command to build 2-hop citation neighborhoods. Produce results/phase1/citation_graph_report.json with: (a) at least 40 papers in the citation neighborhood, (b) identified cross-domain techniques from: extremal length theory, quadratic differentials, capacity methods, computational conformal mapping, free boundary problems, shape optimization, (c) at least 7 actionable leads ranked by relevance with specific hypothesized application to tightening B_u bounds, (d) identification of any recent (2020+) papers in the neighborhood that cite the core references.

items.description: Implement high-precision numerical computation of B_f for univalent functions using conformal mapping
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase2/compute_Bf.py (Python, using mpmath for arbitrary precision and numpy/scipy for fast numerics) that: (a) given a univalent f on the disk, computes B_f by finding the largest disk in f(D) on which f^{-1} is single-valued (i.e., the largest schlicht disk), using boundary tracing and winding number methods, (b) verifies B_f = 1 for f(z) = z, (c) computes B_f for the Koebe function K(z) = z/(1-z)^2 (expected B_f = 1/4 from Koebe 1/4 theorem -- note: this is the largest disk centered at f(0)=0 contained in f(D)), (d) computes B_f for at least 5 classical univalent functions: rotated Koebe, z/(1-z), z - z^2/2, z/(1-z^2), starlike functions z*exp(-2t*z) for various t, (e) handles precision control via mpmath.mp.dps setting. Output stored in results/phase2/baseline_Bf_values.json with function name, analytic B_f if known, computed B_f, precision digits, and computation time.

items.description: Reproduce Skinner's lower bound argument computationally step-by-step
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase2/reproduce_skinner.py that: (a) implements the chain of inequalities from Skinner 2009 using mpmath interval arithmetic (mpi) for guaranteed bounds, (b) reproduces each intermediate inequality: the subordination lemma, the B(r) lower bound function, the C(r) improvement step, (c) outputs the final certified numerical value and confirms it matches or exceeds 0.5708858, (d) identifies the single tightest step in the chain (the bottleneck inequality). Produce results/phase2/skinner_reproduction.json with step-by-step intermediate values, error bounds at each step, and the identified bottleneck. If exact reproduction requires symbolic computation, implement in SymPy alongside the numerical version.

items.description: Build conformal mapping and domain analysis toolkit for extremal domain exploration
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase2/conformal_toolkit.py providing: (a) numerical Schwarz-Christoffel mapping for polygonal domains (wrapping scipy or implementing Driscoll-Trefethen), (b) Riemann mapping of slit-disk domains (disk minus radial or arc slits) using integral equation methods, (c) computation of the hyperbolic metric lambda_Omega(w)|dw| at any point in a simply connected domain Omega, (d) computation of the inradius (largest inscribed disk centered at a given point) in a domain, (e) computation of the conformal radius R(Omega, w_0) = |phi'(0)|^{-1} where phi maps D onto Omega with phi(0) = w_0, (f) unit tests verifying: conformal radius of D at 0 is 1, conformal radius of half-plane at i is 2, inradius of the Koebe domain at 0 is 1/4. Toolkit must be importable by later scripts.

items.description: Establish historical bounds table and improvement metrics against prior work
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase2/metrics_framework.md and results/phase2/bounds_table.json documenting: (a) complete historical timeline of B_u bounds: Robinson 1935 (first lower bound), Beller-Hummel 1985 (improved lower), Skinner 2009 (B_u > 0.5708858), Goodman 1945 (first non-trivial upper), Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2009 (B_u <= 0.6564), with exact values, years, and references from sources.bib, (b) hierarchy of related constants with best known values: B in [0.4333, 0.4719], B_l > 1/2 + 10^{-335}, L in (1/2 + 10^{-335}, 0.5433], B_u in (0.5708858, 0.6564], (c) definition of improvement metric: absolute delta over best known bound AND relative reduction of the gap (0.6564 - 0.5708858 = 0.0855), (d) threshold for 'non-trivial improvement': any certified improvement in the 7th decimal place or beyond for the lower bound (i.e., proving B_u > 0.57089).

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve to generate cross-domain concept tree for the univalent Bloch constant problem
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve evolve with topic: 'Tightening bounds on the univalent Bloch constant B_u: variational methods for schlicht functions, extremal domain construction via slit disks, conformal welding for upper bounds, Polya-Chebotarev minimal capacity, Schwarz-Pick distortion refinements, Grunsky inequality applications, quadratic differential methods, computational interval arithmetic certification'. Verify results/concept_evolve/tree/index.json exists with at least 10 concept folders, each containing concept.json and README.md. Verify results/concept_evolve/semantic_bridge.json has nodes and edges with at least 15 edges. Verify results/concept_evolve/steering_directions.json has at least 5 steering directions.

items.description: Strategy A (Lower Bound): Sharpen Skinner's argument by replacing bottleneck inequalities with tighter estimates
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/strategy_A_sharpen_skinner.py and results/phase3/strategy_A_analysis.md: (a) starting from the bottleneck inequality identified in item_008, systematically replace each loose step with a tighter version using: (i) sharper Koebe distortion bounds from the Fekete-Szego inequality for |a_3 - alpha*a_2^2|, (ii) improved growth theorem estimates incorporating second-order coefficient information, (iii) area-theorem-based refinements using Grunsky coefficients, (b) implement each replacement in mpmath interval arithmetic, (c) report the new lower bound obtained after each tightening. Produce results/phase3/strategy_A_results.json with: old bound, new bound after each tightening step, cumulative improvement, and whether the result is rigorously certified. Target: B_u > 0.5709 (improvement in the 5th decimal place).

items.description: Strategy B (Lower Bound): Variational optimization over truncated coefficient sequences for univalent functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/strategy_B_variational.py: (a) parametrize class S via truncated Taylor coefficients (a_2, a_3, ..., a_N) for N = 10, 20, 50, subject to de Branges constraints |a_n| <= n and Grunsky necessary conditions for univalence, (b) for each coefficient vector, compute B_f numerically using the toolkit from item_009, (c) formulate inf B_f as a constrained optimization problem and solve using: (i) COBYLA/SLSQP for smooth optimization, (ii) differential evolution for global search, (iii) basin-hopping for escaping local minima, (d) identify the coefficient sequence minimizing B_f, report its B_f value and whether it falls below or above 0.5708858. Produce results/phase3/strategy_B_results.json with: best extremal coefficients found, computed B_f, optimization method, convergence diagnostics. If inf B_f found numerically is significantly above 0.5708858, this provides evidence that the lower bound can be raised.

items.description: Strategy C (Upper Bound): Computational construction of slit-disk domains minimizing the schlicht Bloch radius
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/strategy_C_upper_bound.py: (a) parametrize slit-disk domains as D minus k radial or arc slits (k = 1, 2, 3, 4) with slit positions, lengths, and orientations as free parameters, (b) for each domain Omega, compute the Riemann map f: D -> Omega with f'(0) = 1 using the conformal toolkit (item_009), then compute B_f, (c) minimize B_f over slit parameters using numerical optimization, (d) compare with Carroll-Ortega-Cerda's harmonically symmetric 4-slit domain, (e) explore whether breaking symmetry or using more slits yields a lower B_f. Produce results/phase3/strategy_C_results.json with: best domain found (slit parameters), computed B_f value, comparison against 0.6564. A result B_f < 0.6564 for any explicit univalent function constitutes a new non-trivial upper bound for B_u.

items.description: Strategy D (Lower Bound): Hyperbolic geometry approach via Schwarz-Pick refinements and Beardon-Minda estimates
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/strategy_D_hyperbolic.py and results/phase3/strategy_D_analysis.md: (a) reformulate B_u using the hyperbolic metric: for f: D -> Omega univalent with f'(0)=1, relate B_f to the hyperbolic inradius of Omega and the conformal radius at f(0), (b) apply the Beardon-Minda two-point Schwarz-Pick lemma to derive independent lower bounds on B_f not dependent on Skinner's argument, (c) use the hyperbolic convexity of schlicht images (a univalent image of D is hyperbolically convex) to strengthen estimates, (d) implement all estimates numerically with interval arithmetic. Produce results/phase3/strategy_D_results.json with: derived lower bound value, comparison against 0.5708858, and identification of where hyperbolically-derived bounds are tighter or looser than distortion-theorem-based bounds. Must cite Beardon-Minda and Schwarz-Pick references from sources.bib.

items.description: Strategy E (Lower Bound): Extremal length and quadratic differential approach to characterize near-extremal functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/strategy_E_extremal_length.py and results/phase3/strategy_E_analysis.md: (a) use extremal length theory to relate B_f to the extremal length of curve families in the image domain Omega, (b) the extremal metric for the Bloch radius problem is governed by a quadratic differential; characterize its structure for univalent maps, (c) implement the Polya-Chebotarev problem numerically: given n points in C, find the continuum of minimal logarithmic capacity containing them (following Ortega-Cerda-Pridhnani 2008), (d) use this to bound the complementary capacity of Omega^c, which constrains B_f from below. Produce results/phase3/strategy_E_results.json with: any new lower bound derived, the extremal domain structure, and comparison against all other strategies.

items.description: Rigorous certification of all numerical bounds using interval arithmetic and computer-assisted proof framework
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/rigorous_certification.py using mpmath.iv (interval arithmetic): (a) for every candidate improved bound from items 012-016, re-derive it using guaranteed interval enclosures at every step, (b) produce a machine-verifiable certificate for each bound: a JSON file listing every inequality used, its interval-arithmetic verification, and the chain of implications, (c) the strongest rigorously certified lower bound is stored in results/phase3/certified_lower_bound.json with fields: value (string, exact rational or decimal), method, certificate_file, is_rigorous (boolean). If no improvement over 0.5708858 is certifiable, document the tightest certifiable bound and the specific step where certification fails.

items.description: Use concept-tree-explorer subagent to identify unexplored concept paths and synthesize cross-strategy insights
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to concept-tree-explorer subagent to traverse results/concept_evolve/tree/ (populated by item_011). Produce results/phase3/concept_synthesis.json containing: (a) at least 5 concept pairs with unexplored connecting techniques, (b) mapping from concept paths to Strategies A-E (items 012-016), identifying which concepts each strategy exploits and which remain untouched, (c) at least 3 novel hybrid strategies combining elements from different concept paths (e.g., 'use extremal length to certify variational bounds', 'apply Polya-Chebotarev to hyperbolic geometry approach'), (d) priority ranking of the 3 most promising unexplored directions for Phase 4 experiments.

items.description: Systematic sweep: compute B_f over dense grids of 5+ parametric families of univalent functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase4/parametric_sweep.py that: (a) defines at least 6 parametric families: (i) rotated Koebe z/(1-e^{it}z)^2, (ii) starlike functions z*exp(-2tz) for t in [0,1], (iii) convex functions z/(1-tz) for t in [0,1], (iv) close-to-convex functions z + sum(a_n z^n) with specific parametrizations, (v) bounded turning functions, (vi) slit-mapping functions z + t*z^2/(1-sz), (b) computes B_f for each on a grid of at least 500 parameter points per family, (c) identifies the global minimum B_f found across all families and the corresponding extremal function, (d) produces results/phase4/sweep_results.json with per-family minimum, global minimum, extremal parameters. If the global minimum exceeds 0.5708858, this is evidence supporting a higher lower bound. Produce at least 2 visualizations in figures/.

items.description: Implement and test the top 3 hybrid strategies identified by concept-tree-explorer in item_018
items.acceptance_criteria: For each of the top 3 hybrid strategies from item_018: (a) create a dedicated script results/phase4/hybrid_strategy_{1,2,3}.py, (b) implement the mathematical approach, (c) compute the resulting bound (lower or upper as appropriate), (d) compare against the bounds from Phase 3 strategies A-E. Produce results/phase4/hybrid_results.json consolidating all 3 results with: strategy description, derived bound, comparison against best Phase 3 result, and assessment of whether the hybrid outperforms individual approaches.

items.description: Construct explicit near-extremal univalent function achieving the best upper bound on B_u
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase4/extremal_construction.py that: (a) combines insights from Strategy C (item_014) and the parametric sweep (item_019) to construct the single best candidate for a near-extremal univalent function (one minimizing B_f), (b) verifies univalence rigorously: check Noshiro-Warschawski sufficient condition (Re f'(z) > 0) or verify injectivity via argument principle on a fine boundary grid, (c) computes B_f with certified precision using interval arithmetic from item_017, (d) produces results/phase4/extremal_function.json with: Taylor coefficients to 20 terms, domain description, certified B_f value, univalence verification method. This B_f value is an explicit upper bound for B_u.

items.description: Consolidated evaluation: compare all bounds against prior art and assess statistical significance of improvements
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase4/evaluation_summary.json consolidating ALL results from items 012-021: (a) table of all lower bounds obtained with: method name, value (numerical), rigorously certified (yes/no), improvement delta over 0.5708858, (b) table of all upper bounds obtained with: method name, value, witnessing function, improvement delta below 0.6564, (c) identification of THE SINGLE BEST new lower bound and THE SINGLE BEST new upper bound, (d) comparison against the complete historical bounds table from item_010, (e) the new proven interval for B_u (if any improvement), (f) convergence analysis: for each computational method, how does the bound change with increasing precision/grid density.

items.description: Use literature-graph-miner subagent to validate novelty of any improvements against the full literature
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to literature-graph-miner subagent with the specific bound values obtained in Phase 3-4. Search Semantic Scholar and web for any paper claiming bounds between 0.5708858 and our best lower bound, or between our best upper bound and 0.6564. Produce results/phase4/novelty_check.json with: (a) confirmation that no prior work achieves the same or better bound (or identification of prior work if it does), (b) list of the 5 most closely related results with quantitative comparison, (c) assessment of publication-worthiness of the improvement.

items.description: Synthesize all results into a coherent mathematical narrative with rigorous theorem statements
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/main_results.md (at least 500 lines) containing: (a) Theorem statement for any new lower bound: 'B_u > [value]' with complete proof or proof sketch referencing certified computations, (b) Theorem statement for any new upper bound: 'B_u <= [value]' with explicit witnessing function and verification, (c) comparison table against ALL prior work from sources.bib (Robinson 1935 through present), (d) analysis of the remaining gap between best lower and upper bounds, (e) discussion of which strategy (A-E or hybrid) contributed most and why, (f) at least 8 citations from sources.bib. If no improvement over prior art is achieved, provide detailed analysis of why each strategy fell short and what the tightest achievable bound was.

items.description: Document all negative results and failed approaches with precise mathematical diagnosis
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/negative_results.md (at least 300 lines) documenting: (a) every approach attempted that did not yield improvement over prior art, (b) for each failure: the specific mathematical inequality or step where the approach becomes insufficient, with quantitative analysis (e.g., 'Strategy D's hyperbolic estimate gives B_u > 0.543 which is weaker than Skinner's 0.5708858 because the Schwarz-Pick lemma loses a factor of X at step Y'), (c) whether each failure reveals a structural barrier or merely a technical limitation, (d) concrete suggestions for overcoming each failure (what new mathematical input would be needed), (e) must cover at least 4 distinct approaches including at least 1 lower bound and 1 upper bound attempt.

items.description: Produce final bounds summary with complete provenance chain and updated constant card
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/final_bounds.json with: (a) best_lower_bound: {value, method, rigorously_certified, certificate_file, improvement_over_prior (delta), prior_best (0.5708858)}, (b) best_upper_bound: {value, method, witnessing_function_file, improvement_over_prior (delta), prior_best (0.6564 from Carroll-Ortega-Cerda or 1.0 trivial)}, (c) new_interval: [lower, upper] for B_u, (d) gap_reduction: percentage reduction of the interval (0.5708858, 0.6564). Also produce results/phase5/updated_constant_card.md reformatting the original constant description with: any new bounds added to the Known bounds tables, new references added to the bibliography, and updated Additional comments.

items.description: Generate publication-quality visualizations of all key results
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce at least 4 figures in figures/: (a) figures/bounds_timeline.png -- historical timeline of ALL B_u bounds (lower and upper) from 1935 to present, with any new bounds from this research highlighted in a distinct color, including error bars for certified precision, (b) figures/extremal_domain.png -- visualization of the best near-extremal domain found (boundary of f(D) for the function minimizing B_f), with the largest inscribed schlicht disk shown, (c) figures/parametric_landscape.png -- heatmap or contour plot of B_f over the 2 most informative parameter dimensions from the sweep (item_019), (d) figures/strategy_comparison.png -- bar chart comparing the bounds achieved by each strategy (A-E and hybrids) against the prior art baseline. Each figure must have title, axis labels, legend, and be saved at >= 300 DPI.

items.description: Final peer review: verify all claims, validate code, check citations, assess reproducibility
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/review_report.md (at least 400 lines) with: (a) verification that every numerical claim in main_results.md matches the corresponding code output (re-run key computations), (b) check that all 20+ citations in sources.bib are actually referenced in at least one results document, (c) verification that any claimed rigorous bound has a valid interval-arithmetic certificate (re-verify the certificate), (d) reproducibility check: list all Python dependencies needed, verify all scripts run without error, document any environment-specific issues, (e) assessment of the strongest contribution: is it a new bound, a new technique, a computational framework, or new insight into the problem structure, (f) list of remaining open questions and concrete next steps for future work, (g) explicit sign-off statement: 'The best new lower bound is B_u > X [certified/uncertified]. The best new upper bound is B_u <= Y [certified/uncertified]. The prior art bounds were (0.5708858, 0.6564). The improvement is Z.'
